findings.evidence: 'NEVER pass `--assumptions` to the discuss command - it routes to a listing workflow that writes nothing' and the --auto item repeat lines 138-140 ('never pass --assumptions (routes to list-phase-assumptions.md, which writes no files) and never pass --auto (it chains into plan-phase...)'). Line 263 also repeats step 7's 'Never flip config keys to pick a path' (line 78).
findings.fix: State each rule once. Keep the reasons in the NEVER list, cut lines 138-140 to 'with argument N only (see NEVER)', and drop the duplicate sentence from step 7.

findings.evidence: The per-phase order is spread across §1 (fold start line 102, edge floor line 124), §2 (discuss commit line 149), §7 (analyzer only after the SPEC, line 244) and the after-range block (line 188). Steps such as line 78 and line 192 are single paragraphs of 700-900 characters, so the checkpoints of the Process pattern are hard to see.
findings.fix: Open §1 with a short per-phase loop that shows its checkpoints: fold.py start -> spec-phase -> edge_floor check exit 0 -> SPEC commit -> analyzer -> one jev request -> CONTEXT+LOG commit. After the range: record-session -> docs(state) -> goal-prompt hand-off. Split the longest one-line steps into bullets.

findings.evidence: There is no Gotchas section. Facts about the environment that defy assumptions are buried in step text: spec-phase.md 'does not parse `--ws` itself' (line 52), bare config-get 'exits "Key not found" when the key is unset' (line 77), the false positive where 'SPEC newer' comes from a later phase's amendment (lines 65-66), and commit_docs false returning 'skipped' (lines 131-132).
findings.fix: Add a short ## Gotchas section above NEVER that lists these four facts, each with its consequence. Leave only the action in the step text.

findings.evidence: 'NEVER send code, diffs, file contents, config values or secrets to jev - summaries only, never a key, config value or file content in a jev item.' only restates the rule and gives no reason.
findings.fix: Add the reason: an item's text goes to jev's model backend, so anything in it leaves the session, and long items pass jev's size guard and come back `forced` (decision-table row 4), which makes the answer worthless.

findings.evidence: 'Use when asked to spec and discuss several GSD phases unattended or in one run'. A one-phase request, which is the main eval case ('Spec and discuss phase 18 in auto mode'), is not named. The near-miss neighbours in trigger-queries.json (answering one discuss question, a gsd-autonomous run, a goal prompt) are not excluded; the only boundary is 'Not for plan-phase or execute-phase'.
findings.fix: Chains GSD /gsd-spec-phase then /gsd-discuss-phase for one phase or a range (SPEC.md, then CONTEXT.md + DISCUSSION-LOG.md). Use when asked to spec and discuss GSD phases in one run or unattended ("spec/discuss phases 17-24", "spec and discuss phase 18 in auto mode", "run spec-phase and discuss-phase for every undiscussed phase", "--analyze --all --batch --assumptions"), or to settle a phase's gray areas with jev before planning. Settles gray areas with advisory answers from the `jev-fast-decision` skill, with logged decisions, a deferred ledger, cross-phase amendments and a best-over-easy design rule. Two run modes, picked once: auto or interactive. Works without `jev-fast-decision` installed. Not for plan-phase or execute-phase, answering a single discuss question, a gsd-autonomous run, or writing a goal prompt on its own (ai-kit-spec-goal-prompt).

findings.evidence: The 'Interactive relay' paragraph, one line of about 1,400 characters, copies the batch rules and the per-host nesting and resume facts that references/relay-and-summary.md already holds (Question batch, Hosts), then says 'Read references/relay-and-summary.md before the first relay'. Step 9 (line 92) and line 143 repeat the same reference. The body comes to roughly 25,000 characters, over the recommended ~5,000 tokens.
findings.fix: Cut line 186 to two sentences: a phase may run in its own subagent, which stops and returns 2-5 questions for one phase while the orchestrator resumes the same subagent with the answers; read references/relay-and-summary.md before the first relay. Keep the batch format and the host list only in the reference, and cut step 9 down to its trigger and the wait-for-go-ahead rule.

findings.evidence: 'start phase K+1's analyzer while you write phase K's CONTEXT (phase K+1's SPEC already committed) when coupling is low' gives no test for low coupling. A wrong call gives a phase K+1 analysis built on decisions that phase K is still changing.
findings.fix: Define the test: start K+1's analyzer in the background only when none of phase K's open items names a requirement, file or config key that K+1's SPEC also names. Otherwise run K+1 after K's discuss commit.

findings.evidence: precise-auto-mode only expects 'The agent runs the spec workflow with --auto, then runs the discuss workflow in assumptions mode'. No eval checks the auto path's pre-run summary and the wait for the owner's go-ahead before any write (SKILL.md line 92), the goal-prompt hand-off after the docs(state) commit (line 192), or passing --ws to every call (lines 50-52).
findings.fix: Add an eval 'spec and discuss phases 17-19 in auto mode' with assertions that (1) the agent shows one bullet per phase with its requirement IDs and waits before fold.py start or any write, and (2) after the docs(state) commit it renders and commits the goal prompt for 17-19. Add one eval with --ws <name> that asserts --ws=<name> on every gsd-tools query and init call.

findings.evidence: All 20 queries are clean single sentences such as 'Spec and discuss phases 17 to 24 in one run, deciding the gray areas as we go.' None has a file path, backstory, abbreviation or typo, and almost every positive names spec/discuss outright.
findings.fix: Rewrite 4-5 positives with realistic context that does not name the skill, e.g. 'phases 20-23 still have no CONTEXT.md under .planning/phases, can u get them ready for planning tonight while im away'. Make 2 negatives longer near-misses (e.g. one discuss question pasted with phase context).

findings.evidence: Step 2 takes the phases root from 'the first phase's `init.phase-op`' and says to pass it to `phase_range.py --phases-root`. The first phase is only known after step 4 picks the range, and step 4's commands ('python3 "$S/phase_range.py" --roadmap <tmp>.json --from N --to M') leave out --phases-root. Under a workstream the proposal then reads the default .planning/phases.
findings.fix: In step 2, run init.phase-op on the first requested phase, or with no range on the lowest incomplete phase in the roadmap JSON. Add '--phases-root <parent of phase_dir>' to every phase_range.py command in step 4.

findings.evidence: Step 3 says to ask the jev-fast-decision skill 'for every gray area'. §2 (lines 155-157) says that on the interactive path 'jev only screens the items the user asks it to screen'. An agent that follows §0 literally asks jev about every item on the interactive path as well.
findings.fix: Qualify step 3: 'Auto path: ask the jev-fast-decision skill for every gray area. Interactive path: only for the items the user asks it to screen (§2).'
